Intent:
store: document + pin libraryVisible AllowedIDs contract (H4)

H4 review finding: libraryVisible treats empty/nil AllowedIDs as "all
Libraries", so a session scope that resolves with zero Library grants
would see every unrestricted Library. The restricted-Library guard still
holds, so this is a wrong-default / defense-in-depth issue, not a live
breach.

Caller analysis shows empty==all is a load-bearing contract: the ops-class
admin API token scope (auth.ScopeFromAPIToken) and every server-internal
full scan (schedule registration, generated-asset/artwork passes, the
migration wizard, subscription retention) pass empty AllowedIDs precisely
to mean "all". The dangerous empty (zero-grant session) and these
legitimate empties are indistinguishable at the LibraryFilter layer, so
flipping the default would break legitimate callers (Option A unsafe in
this change).

risk on LibraryFilter and libraryVisible, and pin the current intended
behavior with focused unit tests across nil/empty/populated AllowedIDs
crossed with restricted/unrestricted + revealed/unrevealed, including an
explicit assertion that the restricted guard fails closed regardless of
AllowedIDs. A safe tightening needs an explicit "all Libraries" sentinel
threaded through the ~7 empty==all callers; logged in fixes.md.

Intent:
FEAT-9: file-stability check on the scan path (ADR-0032 §4)

Skip files whose mtime is within a stability window (5s) before any
fingerprint/probe work, so a Watcher event fired mid-write never records
still-streaming bytes as content identity. The skipped file is left for
the next pass; the scan Schedule is the correctness backstop, so nothing
is lost. Gate goes immediately before the fingerprint fast-path in
scanFromCheckpoint's processEntry.

New package-level `now` clock seam (mirroring the existing hashFileContent
seam) makes the gate deterministically testable. New unit test proves a
fresh-mtime file is skipped while a settled file is imported, and that a
later scan picks up the file once it settles.

Existing scan/app tests write files with fresh mtimes; backdate them past
the window via the shared writeScanFile helper and at the two direct
write sites so they still exercise the import path.
